selection: Policy, five profiles, controls and primary metric declared before executing v32 codec scenarios; no parameter sweep planned.

service_policy.fixed_base: initial encoder high target + 8 * framing_header_bytes * fps / 1000
service_policy.rationale: A 50 ms rolling work-drain objective is half the retained 100 ms local age bound; a 2x cap limits service allowance without reading link capacity.
service_policy.updates: After atomic enqueue including dependency/count drops, complete expiry chain removal, and dispatch pop+full debt charge. Hold between mutations. Never refresh merely on an advance/report call or encoder target change.
service_policy.debt: All framed dispatch attempts charged; settle elapsed debt at old rate; no idle credit, refunds or resets. Include debt even with an empty local queue and all pending framed bytes.
service_policy.tail: No further encoder/control actions after final capture. Actual queue dispatch/expiry mutations may continue to update service.

primary_metric: on-time frames at 80 ms buffering, retaining every original source slot
secondary_metrics: source, local discard, attempt, admitted and rejected framed bytes
local wait, tail and dependency-safe IDR outcomes
service decisions including boost/cap binding and actual dispatch-window peaks
matched RGB quality on source IDs decoded in all five arms
attribution: Fixed versus queue service is a complete feedback-coupled policy contrast. Immediate replay of all queue-service-generated packets isolates combined sender handling conditioned on that realized source, including packets locally discarded. No claim that replay isolates queue boost alone.
limits: Whole access units, not packet-level transport
Service floor/cap are configured local allowances, not estimated or guaranteed available bandwidth
Rolling work/rate objective is not a hard queue-age or drainage guarantee
Same random seed does not ensure per-frame pairing after different admissions
Real local H.264; virtual forward/reverse/playout clocks; no Colab allocation
